Feeding Copper

The problem is probably the mix in his bowl, not the dog. He needs one complete food he likes, fed the same way every day, with far fewer extras. You can have that delivered to Bed-Stuy, and it needs no freezer space.

Researched September 20, 2026. Copper is a 4.5 year old neutered mixed breed, about 50 pounds and a bit heavy. He has had gas and soft stool for years, and his vet tests in the last six months came back clean.

What a dog needs What is in his bowl now Why it upsets his stomach Your options The plan Contacts Sources

What a healthy adult dog needs

  • A dog needs one food labeled "complete and balanced" for adult dogs. That label means it meets the nutrient standards set by AAFCO, the group that writes the pet food rules US states enforce.4
  • For an adult dog those standards set a floor of 18% protein and 5.5% fat by dry weight, plus minimum amounts of a long list of vitamins and minerals.4
  • Anything that does not meet the standard must say "for intermittent or supplemental feeding only" on the package. Toppers and treats fall in that group.4
  • Treats and toppers together should stay under about 10% of a dog's daily calories. The other 90% should come from the complete food.1,2
  • By the standard veterinary formula, a 50 pound neutered adult needs roughly 900 to 1,150 calories a day. Copper belongs at the low end because he is heavy and not very active. Individual dogs can vary a lot from the formula, so his waistline is the real guide.3
  • A dog at a good weight has ribs you can feel easily and a visible waist from above. Vets score this from 1 to 9, and 4 to 5 is ideal.3
  • Dogs do not need variety. A steady diet is easier on the gut than a rotating one, and sudden changes are a common cause of gas by themselves.8

My estimate, built from the label numbers above. It assumes half a cup of treats a day, counted at the Meal Mixers figure of 59 calories per quarter cup. That puts pouches and treats at about 32% of his day. Jerky is denser than freeze-dried pieces, so the real share may be higher.

  • His total calories are not wildly high. The issue is that about a third of what he eats is not complete food, and it is rich, fatty and mixed.
  • He eats the pouches and any home cooked food happily. That tells me he is not truly finicky. He likes moist, fresh-smelling food and he has learned that refusing dry kibble brings better things.23

Why this upsets his stomach

  • Most long-running gas comes from food the dog digests poorly. The usual suspects include peas and beans, high-fat food, and frequent diet changes.8 Copper gets all three.
  • Overweight and inactive dogs are gassier regardless of diet, so trimming him down helps too.8
  • In dogs with long-running soft stool and clean test results, the most common explanation is a reaction to food. Food-responsive cases make up 50 to 65% of chronic gut inflammation in dogs, and they tend to be younger dogs with milder signs, which matches Copper.5
  • The standard way to find out is to feed one simple food and nothing else. Gut signs usually improve within 1 to 4 weeks when food is the cause.7
  • The test only works if that food is everything he eats. Undisclosed treats are the main reason these trials fail.5
  • If the first food does not help, the research says to try a second one built differently before giving up on the idea.6,7

Your options in New York

Budget is open and freezer space is close to zero, so I ranked these by how well they fit your kitchen. All of them are cooked, complete foods unless I say otherwise.

Best fit, no freezer needed

  • JustFoodForDogs Pantry Fresh. This is cooked whole-food dog food in shelf-stable cartons. It keeps for up to two years in a cupboard and only needs the fridge after opening. It comes in chicken and rice, beef and potato, turkey and macaroni, and lamb and brown rice, and it is balanced for everyday feeding.14
  • Yes, JustFoodForDogs delivers to your door. You order on their website and FedEx brings it in 3 to 5 business days. Shelf-stable orders over $49 ship free, and smaller orders pay a flat $19.99. You can buy once with no subscription, or set a repeat order anywhere from every week to every 12 weeks and change or cancel it before it ships. Repeat shelf-stable orders usually land by Friday.15 Chewy, Amazon and Petco also ship Pantry Fresh, so you have backups if one is out of stock.15
  • Spot and Tango UnKibble. A New York company. UnKibble is fresh ingredients gently dried, so it sits in the cupboard with no freezer and no thawing.17 It is dry, so add warm water for Copper. It is formulated by veterinary nutritionists and meets the AAFCO standard.17
  • Ollie baked or mixed plan. Ollie sells both fresh frozen and baked food, and lets you mix them to cut the frozen amount.18

JustFoodForDogs Pantry Fresh in detail

  • Serving size. Feed Copper one 12.5 ounce carton per meal, two meals a day. That is 14 cartons a week, or about 60 a month.
  • The math. A 50 pound adult needs roughly 870 to 1,170 calories a day, and Copper belongs near the bottom of that range.26 Cartons run from 387.5 to 475 calories depending on the recipe, so two a day gives him about 775 to 950.26 If he seems hungry or drops weight too fast after a few weeks, add a quarter carton a day.
  • Which recipe. Any single recipe is fine. Pick the one he likes best and stay with it, because a steady diet is what settles his gut. A variety pack is a good way to find his favorite. Balanced Remedy is their low-fat recipe for touchy stomachs, made of turkey and white rice, if you want the gentlest option.27
  • Storage. Unopened cartons sit in a cupboard for up to two years. Once opened, a carton keeps 5 days in the fridge, and he will finish each one in a single meal anyway.28
  • Switching over. Go a quarter new food for days 1 to 3, half for days 4 to 6, three quarters for days 7 to 9, and all new from day 10. If his stool gets worse, drop back a step and hold for a few days.26
  • Cost. On Chewy a single carton is $7.49, or $89.88 for a case of 12.28 At two cartons a day that is about $15 a day, $105 a week and $450 a month. The Amazon six-pack at $49.99 comes to about $8.33 a carton. The company's own site advertises half off a first repeat order and 5% off after that.15

Good food, hard on your freezer

  • The Farmer's Dog. Another New York company. The packs arrive frozen, you thaw each one in the fridge 12 hours ahead, and a thawed pack keeps 4 days.20 For a 50 pound dog that is a lot of frozen packs at once. They announced a Walmart launch in March 2026, which may make small purchases possible. I could not confirm which New York stores carry it.20
  • Nom Nom. Similar fresh frozen food, now owned by Mars, with beef, chicken, turkey and pork recipes.19 It needs the same freezer space.
  • Spot and Tango Fresh. Their frozen line mostly ships once a month, so reviewers warn you need a big freezer.25

Other routes

  • Freshpet. Refrigerated rolls and bags sold in grocery and pet stores, so it needs fridge space only. Stock varies by store, and their website has a store finder.22
  • Bed-Stuy pet shops. Yelp's top listings for the neighborhood include Whole Pets Market, Who's Your Doggy, Mr. Friendly Bed-Stuy Pet Supply, Oso's Pets and Beastie Bestie Pet Provisions.24 I could not confirm what each one stocks, so call before you go.
  • Prescription stomach diets. These need a vet's sign-off, so I have left them out for now.
  • Raw food. I would skip it. In an FDA study of 196 raw pet food samples, 15 had Salmonella and 32 had Listeria.13 The FDA says dogs can carry these germs without looking sick and spread them around the home.13 The Meal Mixers he eats now are raw.
  • Grain-free food. There is no reason to seek it out. The FDA looked into heart disease reports in dogs where more than 90% of the foods were grain-free and 93% contained peas or lentils. No cause was proven, and reports have dropped since.12

The plan I would follow

  1. Today, take out the easy offenders. Stop the raw Meal Mixers and stop mixing jerky into the bowl.
  2. Pick one complete moist food. I would use JustFoodForDogs Pantry Fresh, because it needs no freezer and it is the kind of food he already likes. Any single recipe is fine. Order a few cartons first to see which he eats best.
  3. Switch over 7 to 14 days. Mix a little more of the new food and a little less kibble each day. A fast switch can cause the very symptoms you are trying to fix.6,11
  4. Hold it strictly for 4 weeks. That food is everything he eats. For rewards, use pieces of the same food or keep treats under about 100 calories a day.
  5. Feed two set meals. Put the bowl down, pick it up after about 15 minutes, and offer nothing until the next meal. Healthy dogs learn quickly. Warming the food brings out the smell.23
  6. Keep a simple log. Each day, score his stool from 1 (hard pellets) to 7 (watery), where 2 to 3 is the goal, and rate the gas as none, some or bad. This is the chart vets use, and it turns "I think he is better" into something you can see.
  7. Judge it at week 4. If he is clearly better, stay put and slowly bring his portion down until you can feel his ribs. If nothing changed, try a different recipe or UnKibble and give that four weeks too.

Watch out for

  • Extras muddy the picture. If a neighbor or dog walker hands him treats, you will not know whether the new food is working, so tell everyone who feeds him.
  • Blood in his stool, vomiting, weight loss, or two days of refusing all food would mean this is no longer a food question.
